statement: A paper strip of 8 equal squares in a row is numbered 1 to 8 from left to right. The right half is folded onto the left half, so 8 lies on 1. The folded strip is folded the same way again. A hole is punched through square 1 and all layers on it. Which squares have holes when unfolded?

choices.misconception: I followed the first fold but forgot the second one, so I only had two layers.
I thought all the holes stay in the left half of the strip, where the folded stack sat.
I thought the four holes would be spread out evenly, one in every second square.
I made the second fold put the pile next to square 1 on top of it, instead of the pile at the far end of the folded strip.

hints: Write down which squares lie on top of each other after the first fold.
After the first fold, 8 is on 1, 7 on 2, 6 on 3 and 5 on 4. The second fold brings the short strip’s far end onto its first square. Find every square in the pile over square 1.
The second fold puts the pile of squares 4 and 5 onto the pile of squares 1 and 8.

solutions.reliable: Track the squares. The first fold lays the right half on the left, end to end: 8 on 1, 7 on 2, 6 on 3 and 5 on 4. The folded strip is 4 squares long, with piles (1, 8), (2, 7), (3, 6) and (4, 5). The second fold lays its right half on its left half: pile (4, 5) lands on pile (1, 8), and pile (3, 6) lands on pile (2, 7). So the stack over square 1 holds squares 1, 8, 4 and 5, and the hole goes through all four. Check: the holes 1, 4, 5 and 8 sit symmetrically about the middle of the strip, as the first fold requires. The transferable idea: record which pieces lie on top of each other after each fold, then unfold by reading the record backwards.
solutions.elegant: Unfold one step at a time, mirroring each hole in its fold line. Undoing the second fold mirrors the hole in square 1 across the line between squares 2 and 3, giving square 4. Undoing the first fold mirrors squares 1 and 4 across the middle of the strip, giving squares 8 and 5.

whyOnTest: Paper folding questions test tracking layers: each unfold mirrors every hole in its fold line, so the holes double each time.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
